correctness.rationale: In the inclusive ordered nerve the nondegenerate cells have counts n, n(n−1), abn for n=a+b; in particular (x,y,x) is not degenerate. These backtracks identify reverse edge paths, and the other triangles eliminate same-part edges and identify all alternate two-edge routes. The tree consisting of the stars from a fixed vertex of each part leaves only fundamental four-cycles, all killed by these relations, also covering stars and K_1,1. The resulting simply connected two-complex is a wedge by integral Hurewicz and Whitehead, of rank χ−1=abn−(n−1)^2. A stabilizer fixes each ordered cell pointwise. In the H-orbit space each optional same-part loop is used once by just one optional triangle: retract that triangle onto its two other sides, relative to those sides, so the retraction descends even though two vertices are identified. Two discs glued to the same directed circle remain. When balanced, the paired retractions are equivariant; exchange swaps the two discs and acts as a half-turn on the circle (it swaps the two directed arcs preserving their orientation around the circle). The quotient is a disc with antipodal boundary, hence RP² and H₁=Z/2. Fixed ordered cells have no orientation sign; the alternating chain traces minus the constant H₀ trace give all the asserted H₂ traces, including −1 for exchange.

value.rationale: The ordinary quotient changes a simply connected sphere model into a space with integral two-torsion as soon as part exchange is allowed, uniformly in the balanced size. This is an exact equivariant classification for a natural graph-metric test family and distinguishes genuine geometric quotients from rational invariant calculations.
